units.title: Domain A: Nature of Science in Chemistry

outcomes.text: Justify with examples that science uses shared methods such as evidence and reasoning.
Explain with examples what a scientific paradigm is, such as phlogiston and atomic models.
Explain with examples how scientists describe uncertainty and confidence.
Explain the difference between repeatability and reproducibility.
Explain changes of state and internal energy using kinetic particle theory.
Distinguish evaporation from boiling.
Interpret heating and cooling curves with particle theory.
Interpret Boyle's, Charles's and Avogadro's laws with particle theory.
Explain qualitatively the effect of external conditions on gas volume.
Explain diffusion of gases with particle theory.
Examine how molecular mass and temperature affect diffusion rate.
Discuss applications of sublimation around us.
Explain why diffusion rates of medicines in the body matter.
Use the molar gas volume at room temperature and pressure in gas calculations.
Define concentration in g/dm3 and mol/dm3 and convert between them.
Calculate reacting masses, limiting reactants, gas volumes and solution concentrations.
Calculate the concentration of a solution from titration data.
Calculate empirical and molecular formulae.
Calculate percentage yield and percentage purity.
Define electrolysis as the breakdown of an ionic compound by electricity.
Identify and label the parts of a simple electrolytic cell.
Describe charge transfer in the external circuit and electrolyte.
Identify products at electrodes for molten lead(II) bromide, brine and dilute sulfuric acid with inert electrodes.
Identify products at electrodes for copper(II) sulfate with inert or copper electrodes.
Predict the products of electrolysis of other electrolytes.
Write ionic half-equations for electrode reactions.
State that a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell makes electricity from hydrogen and oxygen.
Describe advantages and disadvantages of hydrogen-oxygen fuel cells.
Describe electroplating and its uses.
Sketch a voltaic cell.
Use voltage data from voltaic cells to compare metal reactivity.
Describe collision theory and activation energy.
State that a catalyst speeds up a reaction by lowering activation energy.
Describe physical factors that can change reaction rate.
Interpret data and graphs from rate investigations.
Explain how concentration, temperature, surface area and catalyst change rate using collision theory.
Justify the importance of chemical kinetics in everyday life and industry.
Explain that salts are ionic compounds formed from bases and acids.
Explain why salts are solids with high melting and boiling points.
Describe that ionic salts conduct electricity only when molten or dissolved.
Explain why molten and aqueous salt solutions conduct.
Describe the general solubility rules for salts.
Describe how to prepare, separate and purify soluble and insoluble salts.
Recognise that oxides of nitrogen contribute to photochemical smog.
Describe the role of NO and NO2 in forming acid rain and smog.
State the equation for making ammonia.
State the sources of hydrogen and nitrogen for the Haber process.
State the typical conditions of the Haber process.
State the equation for converting sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide.
State the sources of sulfur dioxide.
State the typical conditions for the Contact process.
Describe the nature of oxides.
Classify oxides as acidic, basic or amphoteric from metal and non-metal character.
Describe properties of metals and their reactions with water, steam, acids and oxygen.
Arrange metals in order of reactivity from experimental results.
Name and draw structural and displayed formulae of alkanes, alkenes and alcohols with up to four carbons.
State the type of compound from its displayed formula.
Name and draw displayed formulae of the unbranched compounds containing up to four carbons.
State that alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Describe manufacture of alkenes by cracking.
Describe the reasons for cracking large hydrocarbons.
Describe the test to tell saturated from unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Describe alkene reactions with bromine, hydrogen and steam.
Describe preparation of alkenes using symbol equations.
State that alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Describe the use of ethyne as a fuel for welding.
Describe separation of petroleum into useful fractions by fractional distillation.
Describe how properties of fractions change with chain length, volatility and viscosity.
Name the uses of petroleum fractions.
Describe the manufacture of ethanol by fermentation and by steam addition.
Describe the combustion of alcohols.
Discuss applications of alcohols as fuels and solvents.
Explain the role of alcohols in various industries.
Discuss the impact of alcohols on daily life.
Describe reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, bases and carbonates.
Describe formation of ethanoic acid by oxidation in vinegar production.
Describe the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol to make an ester.
Describe industrial uses of carboxylic acids.
Explain the role of carboxylic acids and esters in everyday life.
Define polymers as large molecules built from monomers.
Identify repeating units and linkages in polymers.
Deduce the structure or repeat unit of an addition polymer.
Deduce the repeat unit of polyamides and polyesters.
Describe differences between addition and condensation polymerisation.
State that plastics are made from polymers.
Describe how properties of plastics suit their uses.
Describe environmental problems caused by plastics.
Describe the structure of nylon and PET.
State that PET can be recycled back into its monomers.
Outline the importance of polymers in textiles.
Describe proteins as natural polyamides.
Draw the general structure of proteins.
Explain sources, uses and structure of proteins, carbohydrates and fats.
Describe the importance of nucleic acids.
Explain vitamins, their sources and roles.
Identify applications of biochemistry in testing, gene therapy and cloning.
Name fossil fuels: coal, natural gas and petroleum.
Name methane as the main constituent of natural gas.
State that petroleum is a mixture of hydrocarbons.
Explain with examples the types of chemical hazards in the lab and safety precautions.
Recognise the meaning of different chemical hazard symbols.
Recognise the importance of personal protective equipment in lab work.
Locate the nearest fire extinguisher and emergency exits.
Show awareness of emergency procedures in the lab.
Identify apparatus from diagrams or descriptions.
Draw, complete or label diagrams of apparatus.
Explain the use of common apparatus and techniques.
Select the most appropriate apparatus or method for a task.
Describe tests: qualitative, gas and other tests.
Describe techniques used to make sure results are reliable.
Carry out supervised tests: water test, acid reactions, redox tests, melting and boiling points, displacements and temperature changes.
Carry out separation and purification: crystallisation, distillation, chromatography and electrolysis.
Suggest the most appropriate apparatus or method for an experiment.
Describe experimental procedures.
Take readings from apparatus.
Take enough observations or measurements.
Record qualitative observations from chemical tests.
Record observations and measurements with appropriate units.
Record the results of an experiment.
Process experiment results to reach a conclusion.
Predict expected results.
Interpret and evaluate experimental observations.
Process data for further calculation.
Present data graphically.
Analyse and interpret observations and data.
Form conclusions justified by evidence.
Evaluate the quality of observations and data.
Identify potential sources of error in an experiment.
Assess limitations of an experimental design.
Evaluate experimental arrangements and methods.
Suggest improvements to the apparatus and procedure.
